laws: Sites are ZMod N for a finite periodic chain with N > 0.
Constant configurations are well-defined on every site.
description: Finite one-dimensional periodic-chain carrier and configuration type; it makes no thermodynamic-limit claim.

laws: forwardDifference chain q i = q (i + 1) - q i.
The finite sum of forwardDifference over all periodic sites is zero.
description: Transparent forward difference and its exact telescoping finite-sum identity.

laws: Each site mass is strictly positive.
A mass configuration is a dimensionless site-indexed scalar field, not a physical-unit declaration.
description: Strictly positive real-valued site masses, independent of any optional disorder probability law.

laws: Mass and inverse-mass pointwise actions cancel.
Inverse-square-root actions are defined from positive masses.
The kinetic quadratic energy is nonnegative.
description: Pointwise mass, inverse-mass, square-root, and inverse-square-root operations with proved algebraic positivity laws.

laws: The finite Hamiltonian is the kinetic plus nearest-neighbour harmonic plus polynomial interaction energy.
All sums range over the finite periodic chain.
empirical_inputs: polynomial degree and coupling are explicit parameters
description: Transparent finite-chain energy definition; no coercivity or long-time conclusion is bundled into it.

laws: For epsilon > 0, q = sqrt(epsilon) Q and p = sqrt(epsilon) P factor the Hamiltonian as epsilon times the rescaled Hamiltonian.
The effective coupling is g = lambda * epsilon^((n - 2)/2).
empirical_inputs: epsilon is an explicit positive energy-density parameter
description: Exact finite-dimensional algebraic rescaling only; it does not identify a thermalization time.

laws: For nonzero lambda and positive epsilon, g^-2 = lambda^-2 * epsilon^(2 - n).
The result is labeled algebraic and has no kinetic interpretation by itself.
description: Explicit nonzero-hypothesis inverse-square algebra for the effective coupling.

laws: Mass-normalized coordinates use the positive square-root mass actions from Lattice.
effectiveTime g t = g^2 * t is a transparent change of time variable.
This coordinate/time conversion asserts no microscopic or kinetic limit.
description: Mass normalization and the algebraic time-change map live with Hamiltonian scaling, while effective-ODE claims remain in KineticRescaling.

laws: Phi is Hermitian and positive semidefinite.
The constant translation configuration is a zero mode.
description: Finite real mass-weighted harmonic operator and its proved matrix certificates; it asserts no localization result.

laws: Mode frequency squares are nonnegative.
A normal-mode datum is a finite spectral decomposition interface for the proved operator.
Diagonalization alone implies no localization claim.
description: A transparent finite spectral-data interface whose certificates concern only the already-defined operator.

laws: Each modal energy is nonnegative when its frequency square is nonnegative.
Under the stated harmonic coordinate equation, every modal energy is constant in time.
description: Conditional modal-energy conservation derived from an explicit harmonic trajectory predicate, grounded by the admitted harmonic-oscillator conservation law.

laws: Late-window average integrates over [mu*T,T] with 0 <= mu < 1 and T > 0.
Window averages of pointwise nonnegative modal energies are nonnegative.
Normalized positive-energy weights are nonnegative and sum to one.
empirical_inputs: window fraction mu and observation time T are explicit inputs
description: Finite monitored-mode late-window observables and normalized weights; no ergodicity or eventual occurrence is claimed.

laws: Uniform weights on a nonempty finite mode type sum to one.
Approximate equipartition is the finite L1-distance criterion to uniform weights.
The predicate asserts neither ergodicity nor eventual occurrence.
description: A finite diagnostic predicate for closeness to uniform modal-energy weights.

laws: Spectral entropy uses Real.negMulLog so a zero weight contributes zero.
For nonnegative normalized finite weights, spectral entropy is nonnegative.
For a nonempty finite type, uniform weights have entropy log(cardinality).
Entropy deficit and participation number are diagnostic definitions only.
description: Finite spectral-entropy, deficit, and participation diagnostics with only their elementary exact laws.

laws: Continuous first hitting is an ENNReal infimum over nonnegative real times.
An empty event has hitting time infinity.
Event inclusion gives the stated monotonicity direction.
Pre-hitting order conclusions do not assume infimum attainment.
description: Generic continuous-time event and approximate-equipartition event semantics without an unconditional attainment or occurrence claim.

laws: PersistentAfter P tau means P holds at every time t >= tau.
Persistence time is the continuous first-hitting time of PersistentAfter.
Empty persistent events yield infinity.
description: Persistence semantics separated from ordinary first hitting and stated entirely through explicit events.

laws: The effective vector field is g^2 times a g-independent collision operator.
Given explicit effective-IVP uniqueness, D_g(t) = D_1(g^2*t).
This theorem concerns only the assumed effective ODE.
empirical_inputs: collision operator and IVP uniqueness are explicit effective-model hypotheses
description: Conditional time-rescaling theorem for an effective kinetic ODE, not a derivation from microscopic dynamics.

laws: For g != 0 and an explicit event equivalence P_g(t) iff P_1(g^2*t), hitting times scale by the inverse ENNReal factor of g^2.
The event-transport hypothesis is not inferred from the microscopic model.
description: Order-theoretic transport of a proved event equivalence under positive time dilation.

laws: MicroscopicScalingConjecture is a named definition of Prop with no constructor or proof-producing declaration.
It records the g^-2 asymptotic only as an open microscopic contract.
empirical_inputs: weak-nonlinearity, random-phase, resonance, and thermodynamic-limit regime
description: An intentionally uninhabited Prop definition; it neither assumes nor proves microscopic equilibration-time scaling.

laws: The finite phase-space vector field is computed from the locked lattice Hamiltonian.
Its coordinate form uses the interaction force and inverse site masses.
A transparent adapter identifies the trajectory predicate with the admitted Physlib Hamilton-equation operator.
The vector field is polynomial and locally Lipschitz in finite dimension.
description: Transparent finite-N Hamiltonian vector field only; it does not make a kinetic-limit, equilibration, or global-existence claim.

laws: Every finite initial phase point has a locally defined trajectory solving the explicit vector field.
Such a local trajectory is unique on overlapping local intervals.
description: Local ODE existence and uniqueness obtained from the proved finite-dimensional regularity certificate.

laws: Every explicit microscopic trajectory conserves the finite lattice Hamiltonian.
Every explicit microscopic trajectory conserves total canonical momentum.
Neither result extends the local trajectory or asserts thermalization.
description: Proved conservation identities obtained from the coordinate equations for local finite-N trajectories.
